categories.main_business_segments: Corteva operates through two primary business segments: Seed and Crop Protection. The Seed segment develops and supplies commercial seed with advanced germplasm and traits for optimal yield, serving markets including North America corn and soybeans, Europe corn and sunflower, and Brazil, India, South Africa and Argentina corn. The Crop Protection segment supplies products to protect crop yields against weeds, insects, disease, and improve overall crop health through herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, and nitrogen management solutions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Corteva employs advanced breeding technologies to produce hybrids and varieties with superior field performance, biotechnology to introduce traits enhancing crop characteristics, and advanced analytics with digital solutions for agronomic recommendations. The company utilizes a combination of owned production facilities and third-party contract growers for seed production, while crop protection products are manufactured through both internal facilities and contract manufacturers using active ingredients, specialty intermediates, and technical grade chemicals sourced regionally with global oversight.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Corteva serves global farmers across approximately 140 countries, with primary customers being commercial farmers in North America, Latin America, Europe, Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific regions. The company operates through multiple distribution channels including the Pioneer direct sales agency model, regional brands, retail brands through distributors and agricultural cooperatives, and licensing arrangements. Key end markets include corn, soybeans, cotton, canola, sunflower, and other crops requiring seed and crop protection solutions.
categories.geographic_coverage: Corteva operates globally with significant presence in North America (48% of 2022 net sales), EMEA (19%), Latin America (25%), and Asia-Pacific (8%). The company maintains 85 manufacturing sites distributed across these regions: 46 in North America, 14 in EMEA, 18 in Latin America, and 7 in Asia-Pacific. Major sales markets include the United States, Canada, Brazil, Eurozone countries, and other international markets, with headquarters in Indianapolis, Indiana and a global business center in Johnston, Iowa.
categories.supply_chain_position: Corteva operates across the agricultural supply chain as a midstream to downstream provider, developing and manufacturing seed and crop protection products for direct sale to farmers and through distribution channels. The company contracts with third-party seed growers globally while maintaining owned production facilities, and sources raw materials including chlorinated pyridines, specialty intermediates, and active ingredients through long-term contracts with multiple suppliers, positioning itself between input suppliers and end-user farmers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Corteva prioritizes advancing its science-based innovation pipeline focused on delivering differentiated and sustainably advantaged solutions for global food security and climate change. Strategic priorities include portfolio simplification in core markets and crops, achieving royalty neutrality, improving product mix with differentiation and yield advantage, and operational improvements through price and productivity actions. The company invests significantly in R&D (7% of net sales in 2022) with focus on new trait technologies, biological tools through acquisitions like Stoller and Symborg, and digital agronomy solutions.
categories.revenue_model: Corteva generates revenue primarily through product sales of seed and crop protection chemicals to farmers, agricultural distributors, cooperatives, and dealers. The company employs a multi-channel distribution strategy including direct sales through the Pioneer agency model, regional and retail brands, and licensing of traits and germplasm to third parties. Revenue is seasonal, with approximately 65% generated in the first half of the calendar year during northern hemisphere planting season and 35% in the second half from southern hemisphere seed sales.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Corteva competes globally with major competitors including BASF, Bayer, FMC, Syngenta, and ChemChina, as well as regional seed companies and generic crop protection manufacturers. The company positions itself as a leader in germplasm and trait technology, competing on innovation, quality, cost competitiveness, and holistic solution offerings. Corteva holds approximately 5,900 U.S. patents and 11,300 active patents outside the U.S., with one of the broadest and most productive new product pipelines in the agriculture industry.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Corteva is a large-cap publicly traded company with 2022 net sales of $17.5 billion, up 11% from $15.7 billion in 2021, demonstrating strong growth trajectory. Operating EBITDA was $3.2 billion in 2022 versus $2.6 billion in 2021. The company employs approximately 21,000 employees globally and maintains a strong financial position with investment-grade credit ratings (A- by S&P, A3 by Moody's, A by Fitch). The company returned approximately $1.4 billion to shareholders in 2022 through dividends and share repurchases.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Corteva differentiates through its broad portfolio combining superior germplasm and advanced trait technologies with crop protection solutions, offering farmers integrated solutions to maximize yield and profitability. The company emphasizes innovation in new products including Enlist E3 soybeans and herbicides, Arylex herbicides, and Isoclast insecticide, with new product sales up 33% in 2022. Digital agronomy solutions, direct farmer relationships through the Pioneer model, and focus on sustainability and climate-resilient agriculture provide competitive advantages in addressing evolving farmer needs and regulatory requirements.
